article.linkLabel: Open article: Platinum Sponsor Webinars by london.measurecamp.org

posts.content:
Come for the view, stay for the talks (or is it the other way around?) It's crazy how much King's Cross has changed in < than a year - definitely a vibe in the air with all the new tech companies moving into the area (or maybe its just London summer 🌆)

Insightful evening at Google HQ for the London Analytics Engineering meet-up. Key takeaways:

• James Sean Dickson from Voy: Code is cheap - thinking is expensive. In a world where you can "vibe" anything out of thin air, sometimes the more correct move is to be more disciplined and decide what not to build. 30x more code is not going to be 30x more impactful.

• David Ryan Cox (Lloyds Banking Group): Shared their journey to GenBI and conversational analytics. My favourite quote: "If we only measure accuracy, we risk optimising for passing tests. If we measure robustness and consistency, we can optimise for trust."

Thanks to Cognify Search and Meltano for organising and hosting. I even scored a new dragon plushies because clearly I don't have enough.

Two great days at Experimentation Elite in London last week — Mega Meetup on Wednesday, then Space Academy on Thursday: a one-day conference on AI in experimentation.

Some of our key takeaways from the two days:

→ AI isn't taking jobs yet. Brands are using it for internal efficiency first.
→ Customer-facing agents and agentic behaviour detection have moved from abstract to operational since January.
→ Experimentation-first culture matters more than ever — the surface is widening into pricing, logistics, and support.

Jon Su and Ryan Biggs were there from Snowplow. Jon also ran an unconference session on customer-facing agent analytics.

Massive shoutout to the organizers for putting together two fantastic events!
